newsitem.title: USA: Chubb premiums up, catastrophe losses down in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Chubb premiums up, catastrophe losses down in first quarter.

text.p: The Chubb Corp. said Tuesday its profits rose in the first quarter as the insurer's property and casualty premiums grew and catastrophe losses plummeted.
Net income rose to $192.1 million from $151.4 million in the year-ago period. Operating income jumped to $175.9 million, or $1 per share, from $128.0 million, or 72 cents per share.
Income from continuing operations, which includes realised investment gains, grew to $192.1 million, or $1.09 per share, from $140.4 million, or 79 cents per share.
Chubb said net property and casualty premiums written rose 26.1 percent to $1.4 billion from $1.1 billion in the 1996 first quarter.

It said about half of this growth was related to the previously announced termination of the quota share reinsurance agreements between Chubb and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc, which became effective Jan. 1.
After adjusting for the termination of reinsurance agreements, total premium growth was 11.9 percent. Domestic premiums grew 11.4 percent, international premiums grew 15 percent.
Catastrophe losses totalled $10.4 million in the quarter -- compared with $73.0 million a year ago.
Realised investment gains rose to 9 cents a share from 7 cents a share a year ago.
The combined ratio, a measure of profitability, was 96.3 percent compared with 101.3 percent a year ago. A ratio below 100 percent indicates an underwriting profit.
"This is a truly terrific result in perhaps the worst market that I can remember," said Dean R. O'Hare, chairman and chief executive officer of the Warren, N.J.-based company.

"With a combined ratio of 96.3 percent we have again demonstrated our ability to underwrite profitably in all kinds of market conditions. Moreover, we produced strong growth in commercial and personal lines, both in the United States and internationally."

Chubb said its property and casualty investment income after taxes rose 8.1 percent to $143.5 million from $132.8 million. But real estate income after taxes fell to $1.2 million from $4 million in 1996.
Chubb's stock rose $1.25 to $54 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
